objective: Airline customer-feedback sentiment analysis: (a) per-airline sentiment distribution (counts + percentages) -> output.csv; (b) per-airline complaint-category breakdown of negative tweets via case-insensitive keyword matching -> negative_reasons.csv.

data_inventory.completeness: 0 NULL and 0 empty values in airline, airline_sentiment, text; every sentiment value is one of positive/negative/neutral -> no row filtering/cleaning required for the two required outputs
data_inventory.unused_field_note: the dataset's own 'negativereason' column (10 free-text values incl. 'Can't Tell'/'') is NOT used for the reason analysis; the task mandates keyword matching on tweet text

upstream_artifact_status.output.csv: exists, 18 data rows + header; per-airline counts sum to 14485 and per-airline percentages sum to 100.00 -> structurally valid
upstream_artifact_status.negative_reasons.csv: exists, 42 data rows + header (6 airlines x 7 categories); per-airline sums exceed negative tweet counts as expected because categories are multi-label
upstream_artifact_status.data_profile.json: exists, provides types, null counts, distinct values and reference totals usable as validation baselines

plan_steps.name: extract_tweet_records
plan_steps.purpose: Build the analysis base table of tweets carrying both an airline identifier and a sentiment label.
plan_steps.method: SELECT tweet_id, airline, airline_sentiment, text FROM Tweets WHERE airline IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(airline) <> '' AND airline_sentiment IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(airline_sentiment) <> ''; also LOWER(TRIM()) airline/sentiment for stable grouping keys.
plan_steps.expected_result: 14485 rows (no rows dropped); 6 airlines; 3 sentiment labels

plan_steps.name: sentiment_distribution
plan_steps.purpose: Counts and percentages of each sentiment per airline.
plan_steps.method: GROUP BY airline, airline_sentiment -> count; percentage = count / (total tweets of that airline) * 100, rounded to exactly 2 decimals (format '%.2f'); percentages must be computed on the AIRLINE denominator (not the global 14485).

plan_steps.name: negative_keyword_tagging
plan_steps.purpose: Multi-label complaint tagging on negative tweets only.
plan_steps.method: Filter airline_sentiment == 'negative' (9082 tweets) -> text_l = LOWER(text); substring (in) matching per category: delay=[delay, delayed, late, wait, waiting, hours, waited]; service=[service, rude, staff, customer, attitude, unhelpful, rudest]; baggage=[baggage, luggage, bag, lost, damage, suitcase, damaged, lost] (dedupe 'lost'); cancel=[cancel, cancelled, cancellation, 'flight cancelled', canceled]; seat=[seat, seating, overbook, overbooking, upgrade, cramped]; food=[food, meal, drink, hungry, refreshment, thirsty]; other = matched none of the six. A tweet may be counted in several categories; 'flight cancelled' is redundant under substring matching (already covered by 'cancel') but keep for spec fidelity.
plan_steps.expected_result: category totals (multi-label): delay 2112, service 1395, baggage 1080, cancel 864, seat 404, food 120, other 4239
checks: sum of category counts may exceed 9082 (multi-label) - expected
case-insensitivity verified by spot-checking a tweet containing 'DELAY'/'Late'

plan_steps.name: negative_reason_aggregation
plan_steps.method: GROUP BY airline, category over the tagged negative set; emit all 6x7 = 42 combinations, filling missing combos with count 0 (currently every combo is non-zero).
checks: reason labels ⊂ {delay, service, baggage, cancel, seat, food, other}

plan_steps.name: write_outputs
plan_steps.purpose: Persist deliverables with exact required schemas.
plan_steps.method: output.csv header 'airline,sentiment,count,percentage' (percentage as fixed 2-decimal text); negative_reasons.csv header 'airline,reasons,count'. Deterministic ordering: airline ascending, then sentiment in positive/negative/neutral order, then reasons alphabetically - matches the existing upstream artifacts so re-runs are idempotent and diffable.
plan_steps.expected_result: output.csv 18 rows + header; negative_reasons.csv 42 rows + header

plan_steps.name: validate_and_cross_check
plan_steps.method: Recompute counts via an independent path (SQL vs pandas) and assert equality; assert per-airline percentage sums; assert sum(count) in output.csv == 14485; compare against data_profile.json baseline totals and (if regenerating) against existing artifacts.
plan_steps.expected_result: All assertions pass; deviations from baselines documented rather than hidden.

business_interpretation_targets: Share of negative vs neutral vs positive per airline and ranking of airlines by negative share (worst first).
Overall primary negative driver ranking (by category count) and per-airline dominant driver.
Note that 'other' is the largest bucket => keyword list coverage is limited; report it explicitly instead of ignoring it.
risks_and_notes: Substring matching inflates categories vs word-boundary matching (e.g. 'wait' in 'await', 'late' in 'translate', 'bag' in 'baggage'/'boardbag'); the task specifies substring keyword presence, so substring is kept, but the sensitivity numbers in data_profile.json should be cited if precision is questioned.
Negatives include retweets/duplicates; no dedup is specified, so keep all rows (report row count as-is).
Rounding: use fixed 2-decimal formatting; percentages are individually rounded so tiny +/-0.01 drift is possible but per-airline sums verified to be exactly 100.00 on this data.
US Airways (2913 tweets) and United (3822 tweets) dominate volume; Virgin America has only 504 tweets -> its percentages are low-precision and should not be over-interpreted.
